## Purpose and entry points
OpenKore is a cross-platform Perl custom client and automated assistant for Ragnarok Online. The normal launcher is `openkore.pl`; platform launchers include `start.pl`, `start.exe`, and `wxstart.exe`. Runtime behavior is largely driven by user-editable policy files under `control/`, especially `control/config.txt`.

## Runtime orchestration and state
The main process coordinates initialization, console/UI commands, game state, networking, AI, and plugins. Shared runtime state and core services are centered in `src/Globals.pm`, `src/Settings.pm`, and `src/functions.pl`. `src/Commands.pm` maps user or automation commands into game actions and task creation.

## Ragnarok protocol boundary
The external system is a Ragnarok Online server, reached through account, character, and map-server sessions. `src/Network.pm` and `src/Network/DirectConnection.pm` manage connectivity; `src/Network/MessageTokenizer.pm` frames inbound bytes; `src/Network/PacketParser.pm` dispatches decoded packets. Protocol compatibility is an explicit boundary: version/region-specific receive and send implementations live in `src/Network/Receive/` and `src/Network/Send/`, with packet metadata in `tables/*/recvpackets.txt`.

## World model and game data
Parsed network events update in-memory actor and inventory models. `src/Actor.pm`, `src/ActorList.pm`, and specialized classes such as `src/Actor/You.pm` and `src/Actor/Monster.pm` represent the player and observed world entities. Static server/game data—items, maps, portals, skills, packet definitions—is provided from `tables/`, while compressed collision/map grids in `fields/` support positional reasoning.

## AI, task execution, and navigation
Automation is a recurring control loop: world state plus `control/` policies feed AI decisions, which schedule tasks that emit network commands. `src/AI.pm` and `src/AI/CoreLogic.pm` implement decision logic; `src/TaskManager.pm` executes queued/cooperative work. Movement and routing are decomposed into `src/Task/Route.pm`, `src/Task/MapRoute.pm`, and `src/Task/CalcMapRoute.pm`; pathfinding is exposed through `src/Utils/PathFinding.pm` and native code in `src/auto/XSTools/PathFinding/algorithm.cpp`.

## Extensibility and user interaction
The plugin subsystem is the primary extension boundary: `src/Plugins.pm` loads hook-driven Perl plugins under `plugins/`. Notable programmable automation engines are `plugins/macro/macro.pl` and `plugins/eventMacro/eventMacro.pl`. User interaction is abstracted behind `src/Interface.pm`, with console implementations in `src/Interface/Console.pm` and GUI implementations such as `src/Interface/Wx.pm`; these invoke the command layer rather than directly owning game protocol logic.

## Auxiliary modes and native infrastructure
Alternative connection/proxy modes exist in `src/Network/XKore.pm`, `src/Network/XKore2.pm`, and `src/Network/XKoreProxy.pm`. Poseidon is a separate embedded/query-server subsystem for supported authentication flows: `src/Poseidon/poseidon.pl`, `src/Poseidon/EmbedServer.pm`, `src/Poseidon/QueryServer.pm`. Perl is the main runtime, augmented by compiled XS C/C++ utilities (`src/auto/XSTools/`) for pathfinding, packet handling/crypto, translation, HTTP, and platform-specific integration; builds use `SConstruct` and `src/auto/XSTools/SConscript`.
